newsitem.title: USA: Low U.S. wheat supply should discourage EEP use.
newsitem.headline: Low U.S. wheat supply should discourage EEP use.

text.p: U.S. analysts say there is no need for the U.S. Agriculture Department to soon resume Export Enhancement Program subsidies for wheat.
Wheat supplies as of September 1 are expected to be the lowest in two decades if not the lowest on record.
"There will not be EEP on wheat this year," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst with Man International. "There is absolutely no reason to use it."
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Friday he will resume EEP if needed to compete with overseas subsidies.
Analysts said Glickman appears to be posturing for the 1997/98 crop year and beyond, when subsidies may be needed.
"This has nothing to with this year," said Mickey Luth, analyst with the LaiFa Group, of Glickman's comments.

USDA on Monday will release a quarterly grain stocks report, which analysts believe will show the lowest wheat supply as of September 1 in more than 20 years and possibly the lowest on record for that date. Analysts' estimates averaged 1.767 billion bushels versus 1.881 billion a year ago.

Analysts said U.S. wheat exports have been active without subsidies and currently exceed the year-ago pace. On Thursday, USDA reported the United States had sold for export 15.554 million tonnes of 1996/97 (June/May) wheat as of September 19 more than 15.382 million tonnes recorded a year ago.
Europe recently began offering wheat export subsidies of about $6 per tonne, which Glickman had previously said was too low to spark a U.S. response.
Also, analysts said the Europeans applied the subsidy to compete with Australian and Canadian wheat, not U.S. grain.
"The EU isn't attacking the U.S., its attacking the Australian and Canadian supplies," said Luth.

Currently, USDA has $100 million budgeted to the EEP program for the 1996/97 crop year, which analysts said is not enough to wage a subsidy trade war. But, Glickman said Friday, USDA would ask Congress for more EEP funding if necessary.
